title: Balaam and the Plains of Moab

date.label: Undated biblical wilderness narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The received Numbers narrative contains the Balaam and the Plains of Moab material across Numbers 22–25.
claims.evidence: Numbers 22–25; biblical-text description, not independent evidence for an event date.

claims.claim: An Iron Age plaster inscription from Tell Deir ʿAlla independently attests Balaam son of Beor as a divine seer.
claims.evidence: source-deir-alla-livius (Livius, Lendering; Levine 2003 translation): Tell Deir ʿAlla, 8 km east of the Jordan and 1 km north of the Jabbok; discovered 1967; first edition Hoftijzer and van der Kooij 1976; Combination I i.1, "The misfortunes of the Book of Balaam, son of Beor. A divine seer was he." Attests the name and visionary role only.

claims.claim: Comparisons with related biblical laws and retellings need to preserve differences in wording, chronology, or institutional setting.
claims.evidence: Internal textual comparisons documented in CONNECTION-AUDIT.md; interpretation of literary relationship, not an archaeological observation.

claims.claim: The Deir ʿAlla inscription does not authenticate Balak, the donkey episode, the wilderness oracles, or a historical Balaam identical with the biblical figure.
claims.evidence: source-deir-alla-livius: the surviving inscriptional text concerns a nocturnal vision and a divine council; Balak, the donkey, and the Numbers oracles appear nowhere in it, and identity with the biblical figure is not established by the inscription.

connections.note: Related Peor narrative but reports 23,000 in one day versus 24,000 in Numbers 25:9.
Direct retrospective of Baal-peor and Phinehas; the plague was stayed.
Fullest retrospective of Balak summoning Balaam; he blessed Israel still.
Retells the hiring of Balaam to curse Israel and God turning the curse into a blessing.
Retrospective reference to the iniquity of Peor and the plague.

Matthew 2:1-2 recounts wise men following a star, a possible allusion to the star of Numbers 24:17. Matthew does not quote Numbers 24:17; the star reference is an allusion, not a quotation or a verified fulfillment citation.
